dedupe_keys.name: benchmark dataset for automatic damaged building detection from post hurricane harvey imagery ieee dataport

description: Benchmark datasets for detecting damaged buildings in post-hurricane airborne and satellite imagery, built from public data for the Greater Houston area after Hurricane Harvey in 2017 and released with a 2018 paper from the University of Washington eScience Institute. The vector layers combine damage annotations, either volunteer points from the TOMNOD project on DigitalGlobe imagery or FEMA damaged-parcel data with five damage classes, with building footprints from the Microsoft national footprint dataset and an Oak Ridge National Laboratory Harvey dataset, and the raster layers are tiled imagery from DigitalGlobe or NOAA post-storm aerial surveys, so bounding boxes can train object detection models. Coverage: the Harvey-affected counties of southeastern Texas, with TOMNOD points in 19 counties. Format and access: ESRI Shapefiles and GeoTIFFs, free on IEEE DataPort under a CC BY 4.0 licence, with a free IEEE account login needed to download the files. Caveats: TOMNOD points come from untrained volunteers and often sit near, not on, a building, damage is visually apparent damage only, and some county parcel data used were proprietary. Useful for training and testing damage detection models for post-hurricane assessment and emergency response; related records are not yet linked.
